test_title: SSC CGL 2023 Tier-I Official Paper (Held On: 26 Jul 2023 Shift 4)
subject: general
question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the following sentence.

I really don't want __to pour cold water on__ your theory but it cannot be applied to real life situations.

options.text: To destroy someone's written piece of work
To take revenge on someone by destroying their lives' work under the pretext of bad quality
To be critical or doubtful of a plan that someone is excited about
To give goosebumps by showing a prospect

solution:
The correct answer is: **To be critical or doubtful of a plan that someone is excited about.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"to pour cold water on"** means to criticize or stop something that one is enthusiastic about. (किसी ऐसी चीज़ की आलोचना करना या उसे रोकना जिसके बारे में कोई उत्साहित हो)
 
• The phrase metaphorically suggests that cold water is being poured on someone's warm, enthusiastic feelings, thus cooling their excitement.
 
 
• **For example, **"He had grand plans for the new product launch, but the marketing team **poured cold water on it,** citing a tight budget."
 
 
 
• The other options do not match the idiomatic expression's meaning.

Therefore, the correct answer is: *To be critical or doubtful of a plan that someone is excited about.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **"To destroy someone's written piece of work"** is not conveyed by this idiom.

 
 
• **For example:** He accidentally destroyed someone's written piece of work when he spilled coffee on it.
 
 
 
• **"To take revenge on someone by destroying their lives' work under the pretext of bad quality" **is more aggressive than the idiom implies.
 
 
• **For example:** Out of jealousy, he sought to take revenge on his colleague by discrediting his work.
 
 
 
• **"To give goosebumps by showing a prospect"** suggests a positive reaction of excitement or fear, which is the opposite of the idiom's meaning.
 
 
• **For example: **The trailer of the upcoming thriller movie was so intense, it gave viewers goosebumps.
